solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Fish extra tasty essentially in small portion (5,4)

indicatorNotes.essentially: the essence of a word is its middle
indicatorNotes.in: the extra and the S go inside the portion

blocks.note: a dole is a meagre share handed out
an over is an extra, as in 'left over'

annotation.surface: A menu promising an especially tasty fish, though only in a small portion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extra tasty' reads as one phrase praising the fish; split it, and 'extra' is a word on its own while 'tasty essentially' supplies a single letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Dover sole is a prized European flatfish.

entries.clue: Chicago station record framed by Mark (5)

indicatorNotes.framed by: the mark goes round the record like a frame

annotation.surface: A record hanging framed on the wall at a Chicago railway station.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chicago' tells you the sense is American: in the US a depot is a railway or bus station.
annotation.definitionFit: In American usage a depot is a railway or bus station.

entries.clue: Monitor what initially Stroud Vehicles takes north (6,7,4)

indicatorNotes.takes: the phrase takes the letters, holding them inside it
indicatorNotes.north: in a down entry, going north means reading upwards, so backwards

blocks.note: read backwards, strouD Vehicles holds V, D, U across the word break
VDU is only a set of initials; the entry is the full phrase they abbreviate

annotation.surface: A monitoring report on what a firm called Stroud Vehicles carries up to the north.
annotation.walkthrough: The wordplay only yields the initials VDU; 'what initially' asks for the full phrase those initials abbreviate.
annotation.definitionFit: The screen attached to a computer, showing its output, is what both words name.

entries.clue: Revolting skinned birds before large feline (9)

annotation.definitionNote: 'Revolting' is read as a noun, the act of revolting, which is what a rebellion is.

indicatorNotes.skinned: remove the outside letters, like peeling off skin
indicatorNotes.before: the birds come first in the down entry

blocks.note: GREBES with its first and last letters stripped
L = large, as on clothing labels
a lion is a big cat

annotation.surface: A disgusted reaction to plucked birds served up before a big cat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' looks like an adjective meaning disgusting; it is the noun, revolting as in rising up.
annotation.definitionFit: A revolt is an uprising against rulers, so 'revolting' as a noun names the same act of armed defiance.

entries.clue: Church features in gold with difficulty lifted (6)

indicatorNotes.lifted: in a down entry, lifting a word turns it upwards, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: a snag is a difficulty; lifted it becomes GANS

annotation.surface: Church decorations in gold being hoisted up with some effort.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With' simply joins the gold to the difficulty.
annotation.definitionFit: Most churches have an organ.

entries.clue: Infinity cryptically written as NES (11)

indicatorNotes.cryptically written as: the answer, read as a crossword instruction, produces NES

blocks.note: NESS (a headland) made ENDLESS, with its last letter cut, is NES

annotation.walkthrough: Split the answer as ENDLESS NESS: that is a clue whose solution is NES, which is why NES is how infinity is 'cryptically written'.
annotation.definitionFit: Endlessness is the state of having no end, which is infinity.

entries.clue: Persian cleaner’s emergency transport (7)

blocks.note: the Medes were an ancient people of Persia
a vac is a vacuum cleaner; the 's is 'is' joining wordplay to definition

annotation.surface: A Persian cleaner being the one who calls in the ambulance.
annotation.walkthrough: Medevac is short for medical evacuation.
annotation.definitionFit: A medevac is the emergency airlift of the sick or injured.

entries.clue: Driver’s shirt grabbed by scraggy lemur (8)

indicatorNotes.grabbed by: the shirt is held inside the reworked lemur
indicatorNotes.scraggy: a scraggy thing is ragged and untidy, so the letters of lemur are messed up

annotation.surface: A chauffeur's shirt being snatched by a mangy lemur.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is 'has': the driver has his shirt grabbed. A muleteer drives mules, not cars.
annotation.definitionFit: A muleteer is someone who drives mules.

entries.clue: Freak hollow swallows street in Naples (7)

indicatorNotes.swallows: the hollow takes the street inside it

annotation.surface: An odd pothole in a Naples street that seems to eat the road.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hollow' looks like an adjective describing the freak; it is a noun, a dent. Via is Italian, hence 'in Naples'.
annotation.definitionFit: A deviant is someone who departs from the norm, a freak.

entries.clue: Greenish coin bearing six horses? (11)

indicatorNotes.bearing: in a down entry the coin carries the other pieces on top of it

blocks.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
horses are rides, things you ride; the question mark flags the stretch

annotation.surface: A tarnished green coin stamped with a team of six horses.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Horses' are not animals to find a synonym for: things you ride are rides, a stretch the question mark owns up to.
annotation.definitionFit: From Latin viridis, green: the word describes something slightly green or turning so, like verdigris on old copper.

entries.clue: Game shot late ultimately for bite to eat (9)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: take the final letter of each word

blocks.note: last letters of shoT and latE

annotation.surface: A late shot in some game, taken just before breaking for a snack.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Game shot' suggests hunting, but the game is croquet.
annotation.definitionFit: A croquette is a small fried roll of mashed food, a snack.

entries.clue: Knot restraining the Spanish in the hold? (5)

indicatorNotes.restraining: the knot ties the Spanish word inside it

annotation.surface: A knot securing some Spanish cargo stowed in a ship's hold.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Knot' could be the bird or a speed at sea; here it is the tied kind. The definition is by example, since a hold is one place that lies beneath the deck.
annotation.definitionFit: A ship's hold is below deck; the question mark shows it is an example.

entries.clue: Bishop shoulders barrel we pour intermittently in boozer (7)

indicatorNotes.intermittently: something intermittent stops and starts, so the letters are taken, skipped, taken, skipped
indicatorNotes.shoulders: in a down entry the bishop carries the rest on its shoulders, so B goes last

annotation.surface: A bishop heaving a barrel onto his shoulders while the landlord pours in a pub.
annotation.walkthrough: The barrel is not a synonym to look up; it is part of the letter string that is sampled.
annotation.definitionFit: A boozer is British slang for a pub, and a brewpub is a pub brewing its own beer.

entries.clue: Escapes earth rising within bodies of water (5)

indicatorNotes.rising within: in a down entry, the E moves up inside the word

blocks.note: E = earth, as on electrical plugs; it climbs from fourth place to second

annotation.surface: Water finding its way out of reservoirs as the ground heaves up.
annotation.walkthrough: Nothing is added: the E already in LAKES shifts upward, turning L-A-K-E-S into L-E-A-K-S.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are verbs for liquid or gas getting out through a crack or hole; secrets also do it.

entries.clue: Blimey! Part of wheel and pole articulate (4-6)

blocks.note: a spoke is part of a wheel

annotation.surface: Someone surprised by a wheel part and a pole being described as articulate.
annotation.walkthrough: Blimey is a mild British exclamation of surprise. 'Pole' is a magnetic pole, north, not a stick.
annotation.definitionFit: Both describe a person who expresses themselves clearly and fluently, with refined diction.

entries.clue: BA staff interchanged good correspondence (7)

indicatorNotes.interchanged: things interchanged have traded places, so BA and the staff swap round before the G is added

blocks.note: a post is a staff or pole

annotation.surface: British Airways staff swapping good letters.
annotation.walkthrough: 'BA staff' reads as airline employees; it is BA and a staff, which then swap places.
annotation.definitionFit: A postbag is the letters someone receives, their correspondence.

entries.clue: 1 in 55 obstructing animal rescue (7)

indicatorNotes.in: '1 in 55' puts the one literally inside the fifty-five, giving LIV
indicatorNotes.obstructing: LIV blocks the middle of the animal

annotation.surface: A statistic about animal rescue: one case in fifty-five.
annotation.walkthrough: The numbers look like cross-references to other clues; they are Roman numerals, I inside LV giving LIV.
annotation.definitionFit: The old sense, as in 'deliver us from evil', means to set free or save from harm.

entries.clue: PPE item finished with a fringing of laurel (7)

indicatorNotes.fringing of: the fringes of a word are its outside letters

annotation.surface: A work overall finished off with a trim of laurel leaves.
annotation.walkthrough: PPE is personal protective equipment, the safety clothing worn at work.
annotation.definitionFit: An overall is a protective garment worn over clothes.

entries.clue: Dear campers: with energy shortage, propane’s used up practically (2,3,7,3,8)

indicatorNotes.shortage: the energy is short, so one E goes
indicatorNotes.up: a word that is up in the air is in disorder

blocks.note: a letter opening 'Dear campers' is addressed 'To all in tents'
PROPANES USED less one E (energy), rearranged

annotation.surface: A note to campers warning that the gas for their stoves has all but run out.
annotation.walkthrough: The address line carries the joke: campers are all in tents, which sounds just like 'all intents'.
annotation.definitionFit: The idiom means in every important respect, virtually, as in 'the job is practically finished'.

entries.clue: Scoundrel getting pass for green assistant (6)

blocks.note: to pass away is to die

annotation.surface: A rogue getting a free pass for a naive helper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Green' suggests inexperienced; it is a golf green, where a caddie assists.
annotation.definitionFit: A caddie carries clubs for a golfer, an assistant on the course.

entries.clue: Chicken at first laid onto warm foil (5)

indicatorNotes.at first: what comes at first in a word is its opening letter
indicatorNotes.laid onto: in a down entry the C sits on top of the warmth

annotation.surface: A cooking instruction: lay the chicken on foil to keep warm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Foil' looks like kitchen foil; here it is the verb, to thwart.
annotation.definitionFit: To cheat someone of something is to foil or thwart them.

entries.clue: For instance, bone comprises optimum insulating material (8)

indicatorNotes.comprises: AS OS holds BEST between its parts

blocks.note: as = for instance, as in 'animals such as'

annotation.surface: A claim that bone makes the finest insulator.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For instance' and 'bone' are separate pieces that together wrap the optimum; os is the anatomist's Latin for bone.
annotation.definitionFit: Asbestos was widely used as heat insulation.

entries.clue: Sailor in bed rolled edges of cacao leaves (7)

indicatorNotes.in: the sailor goes inside the bed
indicatorNotes.rolled: the lot is rolled over, so it reads backwards
indicatorNotes.edges of: a word's edges are its two ends, the first and last letters

blocks.note: a cot is a small bed
AB = able seaman; C(AB)OT reversed gives TOBAC
first and last letters of CacaO

annotation.surface: A sailor in his bunk rolling a cigarette from cacao leaves.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rolled' fits the cigarette picture but works on the sailor-in-bed unit: C(AB)OT is turned round whole.
annotation.definitionFit: What smokers buy is the cured, dried foliage of the Nicotiana plant, so 'leaves' defines it plainly.

entries.clue: Spanners, tin & titanium left always with Jeff? (10,7)

blocks.note: Ti is the chemical symbol for titanium
Jeff Bridges, the actor; the question mark flags a definition by example

annotation.surface: A toolbox inventory: spanners, a tin, some titanium, all left with a mate called Jeff.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spanners' suggests tools, but it means things that span: bridges.
annotation.definitionFit: Cantilever bridges span rivers and gaps.

entries.clue: Language really applied to African country (6)

annotation.surface: A language genuinely used in an African country.
annotation.walkthrough: The African country in the surface looks like the whole answer's home; it is only MALI, the tail end.
annotation.definitionFit: It is the Cushitic tongue spoken in Somalia and by Somalis across the Horn of Africa.

entries.clue: Where one is cast as a WWII Commander (10)

indicatorNotes.cast: cast as in thrown, or recast, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: An actor asking where he has been cast in the role of a wartime general.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like casting a film part, fitting 'as a Commander'; it is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Dwight Eisenhower was Supreme Allied Commander in Europe in the Second World War.

entries.clue: Words at back of US magazine Time for long-term residents (4,8)

indicatorNotes.at back of: the words come after the magazine

blocks.note: Life was an American photo magazine
a sentence is a string of words

annotation.surface: The strapline on the back of an American magazine, Time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Time' looks like the other US magazine; it is prison time, and the residents are inmates.
annotation.definitionFit: A life sentence is the jail term served by those who stay longest.

entries.clue: Slight change of units across back of wall (6)

indicatorNotes.change of: the letters of units are changed around
indicatorNotes.across: they are spread across the L

annotation.surface: A small adjustment to the bricks along the back of a wall.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Slight' reads as an adjective; it is the noun, a snub.
annotation.definitionFit: As a noun, a slight is a snub or discourteous act, which is what an offensive remark or gesture amounts to.

entries.clue: Criticise loud music when first husband’s away (5)

indicatorNotes.away: the first H is taken away

blocks.note: thrash is fast, loud heavy metal
H = husband; remove the first H from THRASH

annotation.surface: Complaining about the noise at home once the first husband has left.
annotation.walkthrough: THRASH has two Hs; 'first' says which one goes.
annotation.definitionFit: Informally, reviewers who savage a film or book are said to rubbish or pan it, the verb's slang sense.

entries.clue: Note travellers climbing without principles (6)

indicatorNotes.climbing: in a down entry, climbing reads upwards, so backwards

blocks.note: la is a note of the sol-fa scale
the Roma are a travelling people

annotation.surface: A note about travellers climbing somewhere they have no business being.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like a written message; it is a musical note from do-re-mi, and the whole LA ROMA string turns upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Amoral means lacking any moral principles.

entries.clue: Bone sample from hospital useful (5)

indicatorNotes.sample from: a sample is a small piece taken out of the phrase

annotation.surface: A hospital finding a bone sample useful.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bone sample' reads as a biopsy; 'sample from' is the instruction to take a piece out of the next words.
annotation.definitionFit: Anatomists give this name to the ankle joint's upper foot element, the astragalus, which sits beneath the tibia.

entries.clue: Different females carrying a bundle (5)

indicatorNotes.carrying: the two females hold the A between them

blocks.note: two different signs for a female: SHE, and F

annotation.surface: Two women each carrying a bundle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Different' does not ask for an anagram: it says the two females are expressed in different ways.
annotation.definitionFit: A sheaf is a bundle of corn stalks or papers.

entries.clue: Takes in Charlie and small bird in retirement (7)

indicatorNotes.in retirement: retiring means going back, so the bird reads backwards

blocks.note: a charlie is British slang for a fool, an ass
the flightless Australian bird; S EMU reversed gives UMES

annotation.surface: Taking in a friend called Charlie and a little bird that has retired.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Charlie' is not the NATO letter C; in British slang a charlie is a fool.
annotation.definitionFit: To take in something is to assume it, as in accepting it as true.

entries.clue: One in tank perhaps a printer when out of joint (8)

indicatorNotes.out of joint: dislocated, so the letters are displaced

annotation.surface: A printer that has broken down, perhaps as a soldier in a tank.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tank' suggests armour; it is a fish tank or vivarium.
annotation.definitionFit: Terrapins are often kept in tanks as pets.

entries.clue: Standing on set with heart of steel (6)

indicatorNotes.heart of: the heart is at the centre, so the middle letter of steel

blocks.note: to set something down is to put it

annotation.surface: Standing firm on set principles with a heart of steel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On' is the memo word re, meaning concerning, not a position; 'Standing' is the noun, one's good name.
annotation.definitionFit: A person's standing is how others regard them, their reputation or general estimation.

entries.clue: Over-active lover of Zeus with new god (8)

blocks.note: Io was one of the loves of Zeus

annotation.surface: Zeus's hyperactive lover taking up with a new god.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Over-active lover' reads as one person; split it: over-active is HYPER and the lover is Io, whom Zeus turned into a heifer.
annotation.definitionFit: Hyperion is the Titan god of light in Greek myth.

entries.clue: Cool refusal from Norman city blocking opportunity (11)

indicatorNotes.blocking: the city sits in the middle of the opportunity, blocking it

blocks.note: non is French for no, and the Normans spoke French

annotation.surface: A Norman's cool refusal to let a city get in the way of a good chance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Norman city' looks like Caen or Rouen; the words split as 'from Norman' and 'city'.
annotation.definitionFit: Cool as a noun is calm composure, nonchalance.

entries.clue: Register hair in pickled fillet (7)

blocks.note: a roll is a register of names

annotation.surface: Noticing a hair in a pickled fish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Register' looks like a verb, to notice; it is a noun, a roll call.
annotation.definitionFit: The dish is a herring fillet rolled around onion or gherkin and cured in vinegar.

entries.clue: Leaves outline of what HS2 does (less so now) (5,6)

blocks.note: an idiom for departing, getting going
a railway project literally lays down rails; the aside refers to its route being cut back

annotation.surface: A description of what a high-speed rail project does, now scaled down.
annotation.walkthrough: HS2 is a British high-speed railway whose route was cut back, so it now lays fewer tracks.
annotation.definitionFit: To make tracks is to leave; a railway project literally makes tracks.

entries.clue: Hard slippery things might be painful footwear (5)

annotation.surface: A warning that hard, slippery shoes can hurt.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Slippery things' sounds like the shoes on ice; it is the proverbially slippery fish.
annotation.definitionFit: High heels are notoriously painful to wear.

entries.clue: He composed king exiting edgy comedy (5)

indicatorNotes.exiting: a king exiting a room leaves it, so his letter leaves the word

blocks.note: R = rex, king; removed from SATIRE

annotation.surface: A composer writing a comic piece in which the king leaves.
annotation.walkthrough: 'He composed' is a definition by description: the answer is a man who composed music.
annotation.definitionFit: Erik Satie was a French composer.

entries.clue: Better bandaging is made up (10)

indicatorNotes.bandaging: a bandage wraps round, so the word goes round IS

annotation.surface: A patient on the mend once the wound is dressed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Made up' is the definition: improvised means invented on the spot.
annotation.definitionFit: Both mean invented on the spot without preparation, like a speech or tune composed as you go.

entries.clue: Grandly changing silver for United in a generous way (12)

indicatorNotes.changing: changing money means trading one thing in for another, so letters are exchanged
indicatorNotes.for: 'X for Y' means X stands in the place Y occupied

blocks.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver; it goes out
U = United, as in football team names; it comes in

annotation.surface: A club generously swapping its silverware for a Manchester United trophy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grandly' is not the definition but the word to be altered; 'in a generous way' at the end is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Munificently means with great generosity.

entries.clue: Drug mainly lining gaoler’s storage device (9)

indicatorNotes.mainly: most of the word, the last letter cut
indicatorNotes.lining: the drug lines the inside of the gaoler

blocks.note: ACID, slang for LSD, less its last letter

annotation.surface: A prison guard's drug stash hidden in the lining of a storage box.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': the drug lining the gaoler is the device.
annotation.definitionFit: A capacitor stores electrical charge.

entries.clue: Most rough thickets spread across empty estuaries (10)

indicatorNotes.spread across: the thickets are spread out, rearranged, and go around the E S
indicatorNotes.empty: remove the insides, leaving the outer letters

annotation.surface: Rough undergrowth spreading across drained river mouths.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Most rough' means most sketchy or incomplete, not most rugged, despite the thickets in the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: Sketchiest means most rough or incomplete, like a rough sketch.

entries.clue: Labour with dual winch, alternately operated by fluid (9)

indicatorNotes.alternately: doing things alternately means by turns, so letters are used and skipped by turns

blocks.note: killing the Hydra was one of the labours of Hercules

annotation.surface: Hard work with a twin winch that takes turns and runs on fluid.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like work or the political party; it is one of the twelve labours of Hercules.
annotation.definitionFit: Hydraulic machinery is driven by fluid pressure.

entries.clue: Cold Lane maybe starts in the empty ruined arcade (8)

indicatorNotes.maybe: Lois is one example of someone surnamed Lane
indicatorNotes.starts in: the first letters of the words that follow

blocks.note: first letters of The Empty Ruined

annotation.surface: A chilly lane leading into a derelict, deserted arcade.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lane' looks like a road; it is a surname, and Lois is a Lane.
annotation.definitionFit: A cloister is a covered arcade around a monastery courtyard.

entries.clue: Singer brought back separate gin for Roland? (3-4)

indicatorNotes.brought back: the word for separate is turned back

blocks.note: an informer 'sings' to the police, and is a rat
to part is to separate; brought back it gives TRAP

annotation.surface: A singer bringing back a separate gin for a friend called Roland.
annotation.walkthrough: A gin is a snare as well as a spirit, and Roland Rat was a puppet rat on 1980s British TV.
annotation.definitionFit: A gin is a spring snare for animals, so one meant for a famous puppet rodent is a device for catching vermin.

entries.clue: Whale question in exam right at the start (7)

indicatorNotes.in: the question goes inside the exam
indicatorNotes.at the start: 'right at the start' puts the right, R, at the start of the entry

blocks.note: an oral is a spoken exam

annotation.surface: An exam question about whales, set right at the beginning.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Right at the start' reads as 'at the very beginning'; it is the letter R placed first.
annotation.definitionFit: Rorquals are baleen whales such as the blue whale.

entries.clue: Container joint force west of state uncovered (3,5)

indicatorNotes.west of: in an across entry, west means before

blocks.note: ALASKA with its first and last letters removed

annotation.surface: Moving a joint force west of a state.
annotation.walkthrough: The state is Alaska, and 'uncovered' strips its outer A's; 'joint force' reads as a combined army but splits in two.
annotation.definitionFit: A hip flask is a small flat container for spirits.

entries.clue: Old kipper swimming around crusted item (4,3)

indicatorNotes.swimming around: the letters swim around into a new order

annotation.surface: A smoked fish that has gone off, swimming around a crusty lump.
annotation.walkthrough: A kipper is a smoked herring; the fish is a red herring for the food answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A pork pie has a hard pastry crust.

entries.clue: Editor replacing intro to book to make safe for consumers (6)

indicatorNotes.replacing: one thing replacing another takes its place, so ED goes where the B was
indicatorNotes.intro to: the intro to a book is its beginning, so the first letter

blocks.note: ed. = editor; it replaces the B at the start of BIBLE

annotation.surface: An editor rewriting a book's introduction to make it safe for readers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Consumers' suggests readers of the book; they are eaters.
annotation.definitionFit: Food fit to be eaten without harm is what the word describes; consumers here are people eating.

entries.clue: Lass biting Chuck in comprehensive (6)

indicatorNotes.biting: the lass has the chuck between her teeth

annotation.surface: A pupil at a comprehensive school biting a boy called Chuck.
annotation.walkthrough: A comprehensive is also a British state secondary school, which is the picture here.
annotation.definitionFit: Both describe something that covers everything, as in a global view taking in every detail.

entries.clue: A definition of “Irregularity” in Chambers (11,12)

blocks.note: the surface suggests looking a word up; the setter means a medical condition that is an irregularity
not the dictionary: the chambers of the heart, where the irregular beat happens

annotation.surface: Looking up the word 'irregularity' in the Chambers dictionary.
annotation.walkthrough: Chambers is the dictionary crossword setters use, but the chambers here are the heart's ventricles, and the irregularity is their chaotic beat.
annotation.definitionFit: Ventricular fibrillation is a dangerously irregular rhythm of the heart's lower chambers.

entries.clue: Jack aboard Christopher’s ship fighting artist (5)

indicatorNotes.aboard: the jack goes on board the ship

blocks.note: the Niña sailed with Christopher Columbus in 1492

annotation.surface: A sailor boarding Columbus's ship, which is fighting an artist.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a sailor, fitting the ship; it is the card, J. Columbus's three ships were the Niña, Pinta and Santa María.
annotation.definitionFit: A ninja is a trained Japanese martial artist.

entries.clue: In part, bhuna answers meal choice (5)

annotation.definitionNote: 'Meal choice' is singular; NAANS are the plural bread choice, picturing breads offered with a curry.

indicatorNotes.In part: the answer is part of the phrase

annotation.surface: Ordering a bhuna curry is part of the answer to what to eat.
annotation.walkthrough: A bhuna is a dry, spiced Indian curry; the curry picture keeps the hidden breads in plain sight.
annotation.definitionFit: Naans are Indian flatbreads, a standard choice with a curry meal.

entries.clue: Protective garment is burnt periodically before match (7)

indicatorNotes.periodically: at regular intervals, every other letter

annotation.surface: A garment that gets scorched at intervals before the big game.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface's sunburn is apt: a sunsuit protects a child from exactly that.
annotation.definitionFit: A sunsuit is a light garment protecting children from the sun.

entries.clue: Drink over in prison mostly good for one’s blood (7)

indicatorNotes.over: turned over, so it reads backwards
indicatorNotes.in: the drink goes inside the prison
indicatorNotes.mostly: most of the word, the last letter cut

blocks.note: NICK, British slang for prison, less its last letter
to tope is to drink heavily; over it gives EPOT

annotation.surface: A prisoner told that a drink will do their blood good.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blood' means one's relatives: nepotism favours kin.
annotation.definitionFit: Nepotic describes favouring one's relatives, good for one's own blood.

entries.clue: Hollow bamboo cut down regularly near city (7)

indicatorNotes.Hollow: emptied of its insides, leaving the outer letters
indicatorNotes.regularly: at regular intervals, so the letters are sampled at a steady every-other spacing

blocks.note: to log is to fell trees

annotation.surface: Hollow bamboo being felled at intervals near a city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Near' looks like a positional link to 'city'; it is fodder, and 'regularly' reaches back to it alone, while 'cut down' is a verb for felling.
annotation.definitionFit: The capital of Emilia-Romagna in northern Italy, home of the oldest university in Europe.

entries.clue: Sluggish speech from doctor with boring instrument (5)

blocks.note: an awl is a tool for boring holes

annotation.surface: A dull doctor droning on about a drill.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boring' suggests dull; it means making holes.
annotation.definitionFit: The noun describes a manner of talking with vowels lengthened and words stretched out lazily.

entries.clue: Eggs close to grass repelled ungulate (3,4)

indicatorNotes.repelled: pushed back, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: a reed is a plant close to a grass; repelled it gives DEER

annotation.surface: Eggs laid near the grass driving off a grazing animal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Close to grass' looks like it means its last letter, S; it is a description of the reed.
annotation.definitionFit: The roe deer is a small hoofed mammal, an ungulate.

entries.clue: Mistakes spoiled Cleo’s one text message (9)

indicatorNotes.spoiled: the letters of Cleo's are spoiled into a new order

blocks.note: an SMS is a text message

annotation.surface: Cleo's single text message was full of errors.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: a hurried text is just where grammatical slips appear. SMS is the standard abbreviation for a text message.
annotation.definitionFit: The word names blunders in grammar or breaches of etiquette, from the Greek for speaking incorrectly.
